thread:
IncidentBot: PAGER: latency-steer-anomaly detected in eu-west2 -> sudden spike in cross-region routing to apac (>300ms increase p95), elevated 5xx from edge proxies. Auto-escalation: page on-call.

Alex: saw the alert at 09:12 UTC, dashboards look ugly. p95 spiked for a bunch of services routing to eu-west2 -> apac path.

Maria: any evidence of customer-impacting errors or just latency?

Ben (on-call): I'm on it, taking pager. currently grabbing traces and edge logs. will post quick snapshot.

Ben (on-call): quick metrics snippet from the dashboard:```
metric: edge.request.latency.p95 (service: payments)
09:06 -> 90ms
09:10 -> 420ms
09:12 -> 560ms
error.rate (5xx)
09:06 -> 0.3%
09:12 -> 4.8%
```

Raj (net-eng): pinging region probes now. I see multiple eu-west2 health-probe timestamps drifted ~60s, some probes showing stale RTT values. latency-steering decision logic uses 30s window, stale probes can bias the routing weight.

Kari: if probes are stale routing might think apac is lower-latency and push traffic. we need immediate mitigation: revert latency-based steering for the affected prefix or pin affinity to eu for the hot routes.

Ben (on-call): agreed. Putting temporary rule to prefer regional affinity for production routes for the next 30m. Applying change in control-plane:```
# set steer mode to 'region-affinity' for payments-prod prefix
rbctl route update --prefix payments-prod --steer-mode region-affinity --reason "emergency: latency-steer anomaly"
```

IncidentBot: Action recorded: rbctl route update executed by Ben (on-call). Incident severity escalated to P1 due to elevated customer errors.

Liz (support): we've got ~6 support tickets reporting timeouts from EU customers for payment flows, several customers posted higher-order complaints in the dashboard chat. I can correlate account IDs and send to SRE if needed.

Ben (on-call): thanks Liz, please drop customer IDs in #support-private, I'll include in RCA. For now focus on stabilizing traffic.

Ben (on-call): after the route update (09:18) metrics look better:```
metric: edge.request.latency.p95 (service: payments)
09:16 -> 510ms
09:20 -> 120ms
09:24 -> 95ms
error.rate (5xx)
09:16 -> 4.2%
09:20 -> 0.6%
09:24 -> 0.4%
```

Maria: nice mitigation. We should keep the steer-mode change for a little while while net-eng investigates root cause. Raj, any quick hypothesis on why probes drifted?

Raj (net-eng): initial theory: recent probe agent rollout (eu-west2) introduced a regression where the probe TTL wasn't updating correctly under high CPU. The probe process uses a small in-memory cache with TTL=45s and under contention it sometimes returns stale values. That staleness combined with a rollout of a lower-latency apac edge made the steering algorithm flip weights temporarily.

Kari: ok, next steps: 1) keep region-affinity until we validate probe stability, 2) revert the probe agent rollout in eu-west2 to previous stable version, 3) add a canary for steering decisions and probe freshness metric/alert.

Ben (on-call): documenting mitigation and timeline for customer comms. I'm going to coordinate the rollback now and will post the rollback command.

Raj (net-eng): I'm prepping the rollback. expected ETA ~18 minutes. I'll also instrument probe freshness gauge.

Ben (on-call): rollback command executed:```
# rollback probe-agent in eu-west2 (k8s rollout)
kubectl -n infra rollout undo deployment/probe-agent --kubeconfig=/etc/kube/eu-west2.kc
# verify pods ready
kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=probe-agent -o wide
```

IncidentBot: Deployment event recorded: probe-agent rollback started by Raj (net-eng) at 09:28 UTC.

Liz (support): support tickets note customers saw 30-40s timeouts for payment operations; a couple of them retried and succeeded but logged duplicate events. support flagged 2 enterprise accounts for incident notification.

Maria: good catch Liz. Please ensure we notify the two enterprise accounts via the incident template and mention mitigation and potential duplicate events. Legal/compliance might want a follow-up.

Ben (on-call): rollback completed 09:40, probe pod readiness green. Post-rollback probe freshness looks normal. Steering metrics: no subsequent flips observed.

Ben (on-call): final post-mitigation metrics:```
09:36 -> p95 110ms, 5xx 0.5%
09:48 -> p95 98ms, 5xx 0.3%
```

Raj (net-eng): confirmed. Root cause: probe-agent regression causing stale probe timestamps under CPU contention causing the latency-steering comparator to overweight apac. Long-term fix: patch probe-agent to remove the TTL cache or add locking and add a probe_freshness metric.

Kari: Agreed on fix. Also add a steering canary: route 1% traffic from payments-prod to latency-steer logic with monitoring for immediate flips.

Alex: assigning postmortem owner: Ben (on-call) will own the incident writeup. Raj will own the probe-agent code fix. Kari will own steering canary + alerting work. Maria will handle customer comms with support.

Ben (on-call): I'll draft the incident timeline and postmortem, target STAMP + timeline + action items. Expected postmortem draft in 48 hours.

Liz (support): I've created incident notifications for the two enterprise customers and linked support ticket IDs, will update once we have postmortem link.

IncidentBot: Pager cleared by Ben (on-call) at 10:05 UTC. Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring.

Maria: thanks all. Closing the immediate thread; please follow up in the postmortem doc.

Alex: tagging followups: #action-items: "probe-agent rollback patch", "steering canary + alert", "customer communications". We'll sync if anything else pops. :thumbsup:
